cards.explanation: The answer is among the upright in the assembly, friends. The psalm says it plainly: "…in the council of the upright and in the assembly." That's the place where the thanks are given. I think someone that thankful wants company.

The word is pondered, friends. The folks who delight in the LORD's works turn them over and think them through. That's slow, happy thinking. I do the same thing with a tray of cookies cooling on the rack, except I get distracted and eat one.

The answer is forever, friends! The psalmist says it flat out: "His righteousness endures forever." No end date, no fine print. And he isn't done with that word. He uses it again in the very same psalm, and we'll hear it more.

The answer is True, friends. Right there in the verse: "He has caused His wonders to be remembered…" He's the one who makes sure they don't get lost. Then the psalmist adds that the LORD is gracious and compassionate.

The word is covenant, friends. The LORD provides food for those who fear Him, and He remembers His covenant forever. That word "forever" keeps showing up in this psalm. Some of us can't remember where we put our oven mitts, and He remembers His covenant forever.

The answer is by giving them the inheritance of the nations, friends. The psalmist says the LORD showed His people the power of His works "…by giving them the inheritance of the nations." It wasn't a rumor, it was something they could see. When someone hands you an inheritance, you don't need a lecture on how strong He is.
The word is trustworthy, friends! The psalmist says, "all His precepts are trustworthy." You can lean your whole weight on them. In a world where I can't even trust a timer to ring, that's good news.
The word is redemption, friends! The psalmist says, "He has sent redemption to His people…" That's the best news in the psalm. The verse says He sent it, and that's worth celebrating.

The answer is that it is holy and awesome, friends. The psalmist says it right at the end of verse 9: "holy and awesome is His name." After talking about everything the LORD has done, he stops to honor who He is. Nothing more to add to that one.

The answer is the fear of the LORD, friends. The psalmist says, "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom…" It's where wisdom begins, before everything else. And the more you know me, the more you'll see I started at the beginning of every recipe too, mostly.
The answer is True, friends! The psalmist says, "all who follow His precepts gain rich understanding." Follow them, and the understanding comes. And the psalm ends the way it began, with praise.
